selection_criteria: The 80 most recently published GitHub-reviewed advisories for the pip ecosystem as of 2026-08-07, capped at 2 per source repository and 1 per fixing commit, restricted to those carrying a CWE and a fixing-commit reference into their own repository whose parent is not a merge, whose fix diff is under 400 KB, and which touch reviewable Python source outside tests and docs. Ground-truth spans are the lines the fix removed, excluding spans that are entirely imports, version bumps or comments. Two fixing commits were then excluded by hand as bulk refactors whose spans mark remediation plumbing rather than the defect; the reasons are in benchmark/corpus/labelled-excluded.txt. NOT filtered by CWE: classes no 3a detector can emit are retained and reported as a stratum. Newest-first sampling makes the set post-cutoff for any model evaluated later.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

findings.title: Namespace prefix search uses unescaped LIKE, allowing cross-tenant match

evidence.why: ns_condition now builds `store.prefix LIKE %s` with `_namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix)+'%'` and no escaping of `%`/`_`, and no segment-boundary anchor, so a namespace like `("foo",)` matches sibling namespaces such as `("foobar",)` and labels containing `%`/`_` act as wildcards, letting a caller's search unintentionally (or intentionally, if namespace is attacker-influenced) match other tenants' namespaces.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match loses segment anchoring and LIKE escaping

evidence.why: The new code replaces the regex-based segment-anchored match with `prefix LIKE %s` built from `_namespace_to_text(..., handle_wildcards=True)` without escaping literal `%`/`_` characters or enforcing a segment boundary, so e.g. prefix `("uid",)` matches `("uid2",...)` and a namespace label containing `%` acts as a wildcard, potentially exposing namespaces/data outside the intended scope.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: SQLite namespace_prefix search uses unescaped LIKE without segment boundary

evidence.why: `prefix_filter_str = f"WHERE s.prefix LIKE ? ..."` with pattern `f"{_namespace_to_text(op.namespace_prefix)}%"` removes both the escaping of GLOB/LIKE metacharacters and the segment-boundary anchor previously provided by `_namespace_prefix_condition`, so prefixes match unintended sibling namespaces and labels containing `%`/`_` behave as wildcards.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: list_namespaces prefix/suffix match on SQLite loses escaping and segment anchoring

evidence.why: Match conditions now build `prefix LIKE ?` patterns via `_namespace_to_text(cond.path, handle_wildcards=True)` with no escaping of literal `%`/`_` and no `\.` segment boundary, so e.g. suffix `alice` matches `malice`, and prefix `foo` matches `foobar`, potentially returning/matching namespaces that should be isolated from each other.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: LangGraph: Namespace prefix matching crosses segment boundaries in Postgres and SQLite stores

AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Request body no longer read/discarded before upgrade on declined upgrades

evidence.why: The diff removes the deferred-upgrade logic (pending_upgrade) that ensured the body of an upgrade request is fully consumed before treating the connection as upgraded; now self._upgraded is set immediately and, when there is a body, no payload StreamReader is created for it (the length/chunked branch is skipped via 'and not self._upgraded'), so any body bytes end up being misinterpreted as the start of the upgraded protocol stream (HTTP request smuggling / desync), especially when a handler declines the upgrade and expects to read the body normally.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

findings.title: C parser sets _upgraded before body is consumed

evidence.why: Removing _pending_upgrade means _upgraded is set as soon as the Upgrade header is seen rather than after the body is fully parsed, so cb_on_headers_complete now returns 2 (skip body) immediately, causing request body data to be treated as upgraded-protocol tail instead of being read/discarded, which can desync framing between aiohttp and downstream consumers on a rejected upgrade.

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.

advisory.summary: AIOHTTP: HTTP request smuggling via WebSocket upgrade

findings.title: Client WebSocketReader no longer passes compress, defaults to True

evidence.why: WebSocketReader.__init__ now defaults compress=True, and client.py's _ws_connect no longer passes compress=bool(compress), so a client that never negotiated permessage-deflate will still decompress RSV1 frames from a malicious/compromised server, violating RFC 6455 §5.2 and reintroducing the bug fixed in PR #12976 (test and changelog entry for that fix were also deleted in this diff).

remediation.summary: Review the flagged construct and apply the tool's guidance for this rule.
